subject.title: Feature: Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents

question: Should OpenClaw accept the open candidate PR's allowlist-first `sessions_spawn.toolsAllow` API for per-spawn tool restrictions, or require a broader allow/deny policy contract before landing?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the public API changes a security boundary and durable spawned-session behavior, so automation cannot choose the permanent contract safely.

options.title: Accept allowlist-first API
options.body: Land or polish the current `toolsAllow` candidate as the first additive contract, with explicit documentation for empty lists and unsupported runtimes.

options.title: Require allow/deny shape
options.body: Hold the candidate until the API directly supports both allow and deny semantics described in this issue and the earlier implementation attempt.

options.title: Defer unified policy design
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers design a broader spawned-session, route-binding, and delegated-tool policy model.

recommendation.title: Accept allowlist-first API
recommendation.body: Land or polish the current `toolsAllow` candidate as the first additive contract, with explicit documentation for empty lists and unsupported runtimes.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest available prior-review and maintainer-routing signal for the subagent policy/API decision.
